newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan polling stations close after low turn-out.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan polling stations close after low turn-out.

text.p: Polling stations closed in Pakistan on Monday after what appeared to be a poor voter turn-out for national and provincial assembly elections.
The polls, which opened at 7:00 a.m. (0200 GMT), closed at 4:00 p.m (1100 GMT).

Witnesses said many of Pakistan's 56.5 million eligible voters seemed to have stayed away from the polling stations, either because of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan or because they are disillusioned with current political leaders.
One polling agent of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) was kidnapped and tortured in Karachi, where he later died in hospital, MQM sources and ambulance workers said.
Five other people were wounded in gunfire in the southern port city overnight and on Monday in a feud between the MQM and a breakaway MQM-Haqiqi faction.
President Farooq Leghari called the elections after he sacked Benazir Bhutto's government on disputed charges of corruption and misrule on November 5.
